reason: I want to eat from the garden, so I will cut lettuce with the harvest scissors.
expectation: I expect to harvest leaves for a meal, though they may need washing first.

alternatives.reason: Water might help the lettuce, but harvesting directly advances the meal.

effect: The harvest produced lettuce as expected; I can wash it for the meal.
reaction: A small, reassuring payoff for keeping the plants alive.
reason: Wash the harvested leaves before eating them.
expectation: I expect clean lettuce ready to combine with the ration.

effect: The leaves are washed, so I can add them to the warm ration.
reason: Combine the fresh leaves with the ration to make the meal.
expectation: I expect a meal with fresh lettuce and completion of the eating goal.

effect: The meal completed the goal and tied the garden and preserved discovery together in the storm.
reaction: The two fans and covered window make the quiet payoff vivid; I liked that image.

mostWorthwhile.text: Making supper and hearing the two fans brought the earlier protective work into a concrete, quiet scene.

leastWorthwhile.text: Washing the lettuce was sensible but a predictable repeat of the earlier harvest sequence, with little to consider.

surprise.text: The final image connected the meal to the cold case through the sound of the fans; the actions themselves went as expected.

arbitrary.text: None of my chosen actions felt arbitrary: harvest, wash, and eat were clear.

continue.text: Yes, I would continue to see what happens to the discovery and the station after the storm, though this chapter's decisions were straightforward.
